changes.before: Create a labeled contact-email input with email type, autocomplete=email and inputmode=email.
changes.after: Tell the browser what an email field is for.

before: Prerequisite: labeled inputs. autocomplete tells the browser what personal-data field this is. The email token identifies an email address; it is not the name used to submit the field.

inputmode="email" suggests an email-friendly keyboard. type="email" supplies email syntax constraints; autocomplete and inputmode do not. Browser settings and context can prevent autofill. Never assume a suggested keyboard prevents other text.

```html
<form>
<label for="contact">Contact email</label>
<input id="contact" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" inputmode="email">
</form>
```

```html
<form>
<label for="contact">Contact email</label>
<input id="contact" name="email" type="text" autocomplete="email" inputmode="email">
</form>
```
The changed control remains a text input. A keyboard suggestion and a data-purpose hint do not impose the email type constraint.
Optional: change one relevant value, predict the effect, and compare the parsed attributes. Structural checks do not prove browser presentation or accessibility.
after: `autocomplete="email"` tells the browser that this field asks for an email address. The browser may offer an address the person has saved. Their settings can turn that help off.
`inputmode="email"` suggests an email-friendly keyboard, often with an easy-to-reach `@` key. It does not check the answer. `type="email"` is the setting that asks for an email-shaped value.

This field gives each setting its own job.

```html
<form>
<label for="contact">Contact email</label>
<input id="contact" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" inputmode="email">
</form>
```

The label points to `contact`. `name` names the sent value. `type` checks the shape, `autocomplete` identifies the purpose, and `inputmode` suggests a keyboard.
If you change only `type="email"` to `type="text"`, the field stops using the email type check. The autofill and keyboard hints do not replace that check.

Build the labeled contact field shown in the example. Keep `type`, `autocomplete` and `inputmode` all set to `email`. Run the checks. A browser may choose not to show saved addresses or a different keyboard.
